title: Supabase Auth server library: getClaims() token verification middleware and Auth Admin API client
objective: Implement server-side authentication: verify Supabase-issued access tokens via @supabase/supabase-js auth.getClaims() against cached JWKS (asymmetric signing keys, offline verification), resolve the app user from auth_user_id, and provide the server-only Auth Admin API client used by User Manager and test tooling (A-4, A-10, spec 13 AuthN).
scope: lib/supabase: server Supabase client factories — verification client (anon key, getClaims for JWT verification) and admin client (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, Auth Admin API: createUser, updateUser/ban-disable, deleteUser if used, generateLink as needed)

lib/auth: Hono middleware authenticate() — extracts bearer token, verifies via getClaims(), loads the app users row by auth_user_id (active check), attaches AuthContext { userId, authUserId, email, isInternal? } to the request context; 401 problem+json on failure
Cold-start-tolerant JWKS caching semantics validated (no per-request network call with asymmetric keys)
Wire the auth middleware into the T-009 pipeline slot for all /api/v1 routes except health (and later intake, which uses Q-19 keys)
out_of_scope: User provisioning endpoints (T-017 — uses the admin client built here)
implementation_details: authenticate(): Authorization: Bearer <jwt> required; supabase.auth.getClaims(jwt) — on the local stack with asymmetric keys this verifies against cached JWKS; treat network fallback as a configuration error worth logging (A-10 nuance).
Map claims.sub (uuid) -> users.auth_user_id; reject if no app user row or is_active=false (401 vs 403 semantics: match the reference behavior — deactivated user handling per P-03).
AuthContext is set on Hono context (typed variables) for downstream middleware; no process-wide mutable state.
Admin client: single lib/supabase module exporting getAdminClient() using service-role key from typed config; server-only, never bundled client-side (import boundary test).
Test tokens: integration tests mint real sessions against the local Supabase Auth service (Q-21) — provide a test helper createTestUserWithSession() used by all later endpoint tests.

unit: Bearer-token extraction edge cases (missing header, malformed scheme) produce 401 problem+json (pure parsing logic)
integration: Valid local-Supabase-Auth session token passes middleware and resolves the seeded app user
Tampered/expired token -> 401; token for an auth user with no app users row -> rejected; deactivated app user -> rejected per reference semantics

Verification works offline against local JWKS (no Auth-server round-trip — assert via instrumentation or network-isolation approach if feasible; otherwise assert asymmetric key algorithm in token header)
Admin client can create and disable an auth user against the local stack (service-role key)
e2e: Covered later via T-018/T-043 sign-in specs

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to A-4, A-10, Q-2, Q-21 (test helper), spec 13 AuthN.
Delegated to Implementor. T-005 and T-011 run in parallel (supabase/migrations vs src/server/lib/auth+supabase). Orchestrator owns harness JSON.

Supabase Auth server library: token parsing/verification, JWKS cache, app-user lookup, authenticate() middleware filling T-009's prepared slot, admin+verification Supabase clients, createTestUserWithSession() helper. 401-vs-403 MEASURED against RequirePermissionFilter.cs:40-53 and its own tests (RequirePermissionTests.cs:90/:109): 401 for missing subject, missing users row, AND inactive user; 403 only for a resolved active user lacking a permission. Also removed a `code` extension after a test failure revealed problem.ts documents 'no code extension' for 401/403 - detail now matches the reference verbatim. SECURITY: found that GoTrueClient.getClaims falls back to a network getUser() whenever alg starts with HS, alg/kid are absent, or the kid misses in JWKS - attacker-triggerable via the unsigned token header, converting offline verification into a per-request round-trip and moving the trust decision to the Auth server. Closed by refusing non-asymmetric/kid-less tokens before crypto, resolving the key from our own cache and passing keys explicitly, and pinning iss (getClaims never checks issuer). JWKS caching measured: warm-up 1 fetch, then 10 concurrent authenticated requests leave fetchCount at 1; unknown-kid burst adds <=1 with a 30s cooldown so it cannot be a fetch amplifier. 6 mutants, all killed - but TWO INITIALLY SURVIVED and both were real test defects: the tamper test changed sub so the user lookup masked disabled signature verification (fixed with a sub-preserving tamper + impostor-key-under-known-kid case, 1->3 kills), and HS256/none tokens carried unknown kids so the algorithm allow-list was never exercised (fixed with a known-kid test using a fetch-counting client, which directly observes the downgrade path).

Evaluator PASS. getClaims downgrade vulnerability VERIFIED in installed @supabase/auth-js source (GoTrueClient.getClaims: getUser() network fallback when alg missing/HS*, kid missing, or fetchJwk kid-miss; no iss check anywhere) and the mitigation verified real: fetchJwk returns a caller-supplied key without any network path, so alg allow-list + kid requirement + own JwksCache + explicit keys + issuer pin fully closes the downgrade. Evaluator REPRODUCED the allow-list mutant (isAllowedAlgorithm => true): killed by exactly the repaired known-kid fetch-counting test (1 failed/26 passed), restored, suite green. V-020 RULING: fetch-count substitution judged insufficient alone (the warm-path instrument cannot observe a getUser round-trip by the real client), so the Evaluator PERFORMED THE LITERAL CONTAINER PAUSE: warm-up 1 JWKS fetch, paused supabase_auth_quoteiq, confirmed JWKS unreachable, 10/10 verifications of a valid token succeeded offline with fetchCount still 1, unpaused, container healthy, post-restore sign-in OK. V-020 satisfied by direct measurement; the fetch-counting tests remain the CI-safe regression guard (a docker-pausing vitest would be destructive/flaky). Security: raw JWT, token fragment, eyJ pattern, service-role key and password all asserted ABSENT from captured log output; service-role key confined to config schema + single admin factory with non-empty-scan guards; UI cannot import src/server. DEFERRED (non-blocking, tracked): (a) composition-root wiring proven by source assertion only until T-015 lands /me - must then become a behavioural 401 assertion on a real route; (b) createPgAppUserLookup's private pg.Pool (max 2) is correctly behind the AppUserLookup port for T-008's Kysely replacement. No findings.
